Anya: Ran an Nsight capture on the offending run (tp=2 pp=2, seq=1024, batch=8). Seeing periodic ~6-12ms spikes in the all-reduce window that line up with kernel handoffs. Capture uploaded: s3://redwood-profiles/1869991111/nsight_capture.qdrep. Can someone take a quick look?

Zach: grabbing it now. Do you also have nvprof and our custom-timers traces for the same run? Nsight is great but we need the app-level timers to map scheduling decisions.

Anya: yes attached nvprof summary and timers in the same S3 folder (nvprof_summary.txt, microtimers.log). Command used: 
```
./bin/run_infer --model rwrw-13b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kv-prefetch 1 --capture nsight
```

Kevin: quick glance: nvprof shows an AllReduceKernel tail with max ~11.9ms but median ~0.5ms. Looks like occasional fallback/serialisation. Snippet: 
```
AllReduceKernel         calls: 432   avg: 0.45ms   max: 11.9ms   p95: 3.2ms
Send/Recv               calls: 864   avg: 0.12ms   max: 4.8ms
```

Kevin: also microtimers.log shows gaps between compute_end and next_kernel_start that match the spike times: 
```
[2001.234] layer 23 compute_end
[2001.241] enqueue_allreduce start
[2001.252] enqueue_allreduce done
[2001.263] next_kernel start
```
(spikes where enqueue_allreduce done -> next_kernel start > 6ms)

PerfBot: New processing result: nsight_capture.qdrep processed. Derived metrics: allreduce_p95=3.2ms, allreduce_outliers=0.7%, inter-kernel_gap_p99=9.8ms. Report: https://perfbot.internal/reports/1869991111

Lia: hypothesis: kernel selection / fallback may be choosing a non-fused path for some tensor sizes during the KV cache path. When small micro-batches + KV prefetch interleave with allreduce scheduling, NCCL might pick a ring vs hierarchical algorithm or fall back to rendezvous -> tail spikes.

Zach: yes. Can you try a quick experiment: 1) disable kv-prefetch (--kv-prefetch=0) 2) force fused allreduce path (KERNEL_HINT=fused_allreduce or --force-kernel fused_allreduce) 3) run with batching heuristics toggled (continuous vs bounded). Compare p99/p95 and throughput. Command variants: 
```
# baseline
./bin/run_infer --model rwrw-13b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kv-prefetch 1
# no prefetch
./bin/run_infer ... --kv-prefetch 0
# force kernel
KERNEL_HINT=fused_allreduce ./bin/run_infer ...
# switch batching
./bin/run_infer ... --batching bounded
```

Anya: ran the quick A/B. Results (short):
- baseline (kv_prefetch=1): p99 inter-kernel gap 28.3ms, throughput 1020 tokens/s
- kv_prefetch=0: p99 inter-kernel gap 8.9ms, throughput 992 tokens/s (-2.8%)
- KERNEL_HINT=fused_allreduce: p99 6.5ms, throughput 1015 tokens/s
- batching=bounded: p99 7.4ms, throughput 1003 tokens/s
So disabling prefetch or forcing fused kernel reduces tails. Looks like prefetch introduces scheduling jitter that occasionally serializes allreduce windows.

Kevin: that matches. Prefetch threads are racing the allreduce enqueue path and sometimes we hit a kernel selection path that schedules extra memcopies. Two follow-ups: 1) add microtimers around kernel selection and NCCL algorithm choose 2) try async-allreduce (background launch) to decouple scheduling from main thread.

Zach: can you push a microtimers patch that logs: kernel_choose_start, kernel_choose_done, enqueue_allreduce_start, enqueue_allreduce_done, kernel_launch_start? Keep it low-overhead sampling. Then re-run Nsight for a smaller run (seq=512, batch=4) to keep capture size down.

Anya: will do. Also noticed in Nsight capture that some allreduce kernels are using a fallback kernel: kernel name includes "reduce_fallback" in ~0.7% of calls. Maybe our heuristic threshold for fused path is off for some boundary sizes.

Lia: we should adjust the kernel selection table: expand the fused_allreduce window for dim sizes 128-256, and add a soft-cost penalty when kv-prefetch threads are enabled (so fused is preferred). We can add a dynamic heuristic: if kv_prefetch enabled, bias toward fused kernels.

Kevin: good plan. Also test NCCL env vars: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL, NCCL_ALGO=RING/Tree, and NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1 toggles to see if hierarchy helps. Add a run with NCCL_ALGO=Tree to compare.

Anya: ran a tree run: NCCL_ALGO=Tree gave p99 5.9ms but throughput slightly lower. Looks promising for tail. Uploaded results in same S3 folder.

eng-sre: fyi if this goes to prod default we should add a canary rollout + metrics guard (allreduce_p99 and end-to-end p99) and automatic fallback to previous kernel table.

Zach: agreed. For now actionable items: 
- Anya: push microtimer capture changes and new small nsight run.
- Lia: prepare kernel-table patch with fused expansion + kv-prefetch bias.
- Kevin: test async-allreduce background launcher and NCCL_ALGO matrix.
- eng-sre: prepare rollout plan + alerting thresholds.

Anya: will send PR with microtimers, run capture tonight, and post quick numbers tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Kevin: nice find. Short-term fix might be to default kv-prefetch=0 for tp>1 until we get kernel-table tuned.

Lia: agreed, include that in the canary config.

PerfBot: Scheduled nightly capture job (1869992000) to collect microtimer-enabled traces for regression check.

Anya: closing loop later with final numbers. cc @eng-sre for rollout notes.
